body.p: As of entry of this Response, Claims 1-19 are pending, with claims 1, 8, and 15 being independent. Claims 1, 2, 8, 9, and 15 have been amended. No new subject matter has been added. No new matter is added.
Reconsideration and allowance of the pending application and claims is respectfully requested in light of the foregoing amendments and the following remarks.
I. Double Patenting Rejections

With regard to the rejections of claims 1-19 and claims 1, 2, 6-9, 13-17, and 19 under the doctrine of non-statutory obviousness-type double patenting, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection be held in abeyance until it is the only rejection outstanding in accordance with MPEP § 714.02 and 37 C.F.R. § 1.111(b), as the claims may be further examined notwithstanding the rejection.
II. Rejections of Claims 1-19 Under 35 U.S.C. & 112

At page 3, the Office Action rejects claims 1-19 under 35 U.S.C. § 112, second paragraph, as indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which Applicant regards as the invention. Applicant has amended the claims in accordance with the suggestions presented in the Office Action.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 112 of claims 1-19 be withdrawn.
III. Rejections of Claims 1-9 and 13-19 Under 35 U.S.C. & 102

At pages 4-12, the Office Action rejects claims 1-7 under 35 U.S.C. § 102(b) as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Publication No. 2010/0160943 ("Lamps '943") and rejects claims 8, 9, and 13-19 under 35 U.S.C. § 102(b) as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Publication No. 2010/0160942 ("Lamps '942").

A claim is anticipated under 35 U.S.C. § 102 only if each and every element as set forth in the claim is found, either expressly or inherently described, in a single prior art reference. Verdegaal Bros. v. Union Oil Co. of California, 814 F.2d 628, 631 (Fed. Cir. 1987). Stated differently, to anticipate a claim, it is required "that the four corners of a single, prior art document describe every element of the claimed invention." Xerox Corp. v. 3Com Corp., 458 F.3d 1310, 1322 (Fed. Cir. 2006). Further, "unless a reference discloses within the four corners of the document not only all of the limitations claimed but also all of the limitations arranged or combined in the same way as recited in the claim, it cannot be said to prove prior invention of the thing claimed and, thus, cannot anticipate under 35 U.S.C. § 102." Net MoneylN, Inc. v. VeriSign, Inc., 545 F.3d 1359, 1371 (Fed. Cir. 2008). See also MPEP § 2131.
Applicant respectfully requests that the rejections of claims 1-9 and 13-19 be withdrawn for at least the reasons discussed below.
A. Claim 1

Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claim 1 be withdrawn because Lamps '943 does not every element of claim 1. For example, Lamps '943 does not disclose "a latch mechanism operable to permit the lancet carrier to travel through the advancing portion and the
return portion of the lancing stroke, and to thereafter prevent excess oscillation of the lancet carrier from the neutral position," as recited by claim 1.
Applicant has also moved the return spring element to be positioned after the drive spring element to reflect the order in which the structures
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 102(b) of claim 1 and claims 2-7, which depend therefrom, be withdrawn.
B. Claims 8 and 15

Claims 8 and 15, although differing in scope and/or statutory class from claim 1, each recites features distinguishable from Lamps '942 for at least reasons similar to those discussed above with regard to claim 1, to the extent applicable. Lamps '942 also does not disclose "a latch mechanism operable to permit the lancet carrier to travel through the advancing portion and the return portion of the lancing stroke, and to thereafter prevent excess oscillation of the lancet carrier from the neutral position." Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 102(b) of claims 8 and 15, and claims dependent therefrom, be withdrawn.
IV. Rejection of Claims 10-12 Under 35 U.S.C. 4 103
At pages 13, the Office Action rejects claims 10-12 under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) as allegedly being unpatentable over Lamps '942 in view of Lamps '943.

In order to establish a prima facie case of obviousness under 35 U.S.C. § 103, each and every element of a claim must be described or suggested by the prior art or obvious in view of the prior art. See In re Fine, 837 F.2d 1071, 1073-1074 (Fed. Cir. 1988); Ex Parte Wada and Murphy, Appeal 2007-3733 (BPAI 2008); See also, KSR Int'l v. Teleflex, Inc., 550 U.S. 398,

411 (2007) (claim deemed obvious to one of ordinary skill where all claim elements were disclosed in the cited prior art references). In addition, "[r]ejections on obviousness grounds cannot be sustained by mere conclusory statements; instead, there must be some articulated reasoning with some rational underpinning to support the legal conclusion of obviousness." KSR Int'l, 550 U.S. at 418 (quoting In re Kahn, 441 F.3d 977, 988 (Fed. Cir. 2006)).
Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 10-12 be withdrawn for at least the reasons discussed below.
A. Claims 10-12
Claims 10-12 depend from claim 8, and Applicant submits that claim 8 is distinguishable over Lamps '942 and Lamps '943 for at least the reasons discussed above with regard to claim 8.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) of claims 10-12 be withdrawn.
V. No Waiver

Applicant's arguments and amendments are without prejudice, waiver, or disclaimer. Applicant reserves the right to identify additional differences between the claimed invention and the references cited in the Office Action, although the differences may not be specifically addressed or identified in this Response. Additionally, although Applicant has not specifically responded to the rejection of each dependent claim presented in the Office Action, Applicant submits that the dependent claims are allowable for being dependent upon allowable independent claims. See In re Fine, 837 F.2d 1071, 1076 (Fed. Cir. 1988). Applicant reserves the right to address the patentability of any and all additional claim elements in the future.

It is requested that all outstanding objections and rejections be withdrawn and that this application and all presently pending claims be allowed to issue.
